name: Coming of Age
definition: A young or inexperienced protagonist revises an inherited model of self and society through consequential encounters, responsibility, loss, and chosen identity.
negative_signals: adult transformation unrelated to formative independence
diagnostic_questions: Does experience change how the protagonist understands self and society?
Does the ending demonstrate a new capacity for responsibility?

neighbors.distinction: Coming of age centers formative identity even when family conflict supplies pressure.
A quest may carry maturation, but coming of age measures success by developmental choice.

reader_promises.name: Formative experience
reader_promises.description: Make encounters challenge a specific inherited belief or protected identity.

reader_promises.name: Demonstrated growth
reader_promises.description: End with behavior showing a more complex capacity for choice and consequence.

roles.name: Developing protagonist
roles.description: Begins with limited experience and a workable but insufficient model of the world.

roles.name: Peer mirror
roles.description: Offers belonging, rivalry, intimacy, or an alternative path.

roles.name: Adult model
roles.description: Represents an inherited rule, failed future, or credible form of maturity.

stakes: Loss or transformation of childhood bonds
Capacity to act without borrowed certainty
settings: First workplace, journey, or independent residence
motifs: Objects from childhood gaining new meaning

movements.name: Protected self
movements.description: Establish the belief, role, or relationship that keeps complexity manageable.

movements.name: First crossing
movements.description: Enter a responsibility or social world where old strategies partly fail.

movements.name: Disillusionment
movements.description: Lose an idealized account without making growth equal cynicism.

movements.name: Owned choice
movements.description: Act from a revised identity and accept a consequence without retreating to the old role.

complications.name: Belonging cost
complications.description: Acceptance requires behavior that conflicts with emerging values.

complications.name: Adult failure
complications.description: A trusted adult cannot provide the expected protection or answer.

complications.name: Early power
complications.description: New freedom arrives before the judgment needed to use it safely.

twists.name: Rebel inherits
twists.description: The protagonist discovers that rebellion can reproduce the same controlling pattern.

twists.name: Adult becomes human
twists.description: A condemned authority figure is reinterpreted without erasing their failures.

conclusions.name: Independent step
conclusions.description: The protagonist chooses a path with realistic responsibility.

conclusions.name: Redefined belonging
conclusions.description: The protagonist remains connected while renegotiating identity and boundaries.

conclusions.name: Bittersweet knowledge
conclusions.description: Growth comes through an irreversible loss integrated into a fuller self-understanding.

subversions: Let maturity include renewed dependence and community rather than solitary independence.
Make an apparent regression reveal a healthier boundary.
cliches_to_avoid: Adults existing only as obstacles or wisdom dispensers
quality_checks: Growth responds to specific accumulated experiences.
Final behavior differs meaningfully from the opening pattern.

sources.title: Coming of Age in Hong Kong
sources.contribution: Grounds the form in psychological and moral development from youth toward social experience.

sources.title: The Narrative Arc: Revealing Core Narrative Structures through Text Analysis
sources.author_or_organization: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences / PMC
sources.contribution: Supports flexible staging, progression, and cognitive-affective change across narratives.
